value.rationale: The minimal common shifted-factor gcd is a natural invariant in the standard three-prime decomposition, and the theorem gives a complete cutoff-free classification of that extremal stratum rather than a bounded census.
residual_risks: Because the argument is elementary, older problem literature or differently indexed Lucas-Carmichael notes could contain the same specialization.

disclaimer: Independent mathematical audit; not peer review, formal proof-assistant verification, or a guarantee of first discovery.
final_claim: If a three-prime Lucas-Carmichael number \(n=pqr\) satisfies \(\gcd(p+1,q+1,r+1)=2\), then \((p,q,r)=(5,13,31)\), and conversely; hence \(2015\) is the unique primitive three-prime case.

correctness.rationale: The normalized-factor reduction was rechecked with the required modulus 2d in the pairwise-coprimality step; the lcm step, three-valued quotient, and all three case eliminations were rederived; 2015 satisfies the defining divisibilities directly. A separate bounded exact enumeration found no contradictory primitive triple.

originality.rationale: Relevant structural results of Wright, Tamilvanan-Muthukrishnan, Einsele-Paterson, OEIS data, exact/synonymous web searches, and current SCOPE records were checked. No prior classification of the gcd(p+1,q+1,r+1)=2 stratum was located. Originality remains to the best of our knowledge, with residual risk in older or differently indexed elementary literature.

value.rationale: The theorem completely classifies the minimal-common-gcd case of the standard three-prime Lucas-Carmichael decomposition and singles out 2015 without any size cutoff.
